to give some context around this

prob 90% is typical MBA biz analysis + standard-issue equity analysis
-what makes a good vs bad biz
-porter's five forces
-sustainable competitive advantages
-understanding where a business is in the value chain (customers/suppliers), who has leverage, who controls pricing, who captures most of the economics or most of the profit pool
-VAR is a catch all for any/all primary research and should drive ur model assumptions

there's a lot of questions which are worded in a way to test ur understanding of the business w/ the answer

but each firm has their own versions of these, and the secret sauce really isnt that secret...like a sell-side eq rsch analyst should have close to the same level of understanding, or someone at a LO

I posted it bc its pretty thorough, in the sense that you dont usually know what u dont know

so if u "know" a business but can't answer everything on this framework, u really dont know the business.

the other 10% that isn't MBA-ish, is standard long/short equity ish

ests vs street, variant view, catalyst, event path, sentiment, positioning

and whatever would be deserving of the "tiger cub" label, is really just, "the amount of VAR I've done makes me the smartest person in the room on this stock/sector."

combined with, I have a LT fundamental view thats working, while navigating all the ST events to add extra bps of return/spread vs a short

otherwise ur just a LO charging L/S fees, or its just beta, or its just "we're long the quality factor" + some lazy shorts to bring down net

the biggest change since this framework was written, was multi-mgrs exposing a lot of strategies as factor bets (ie long AMZN, short brick and mortar retail)

this compressed everyone's time horizon and made 20% of this checklist/framework sort of useless...its stuff that matters over 3-5 years but no one has that time horizon anymore

overall this is a good swiss army knife checklist/framework to test ur understanding

but if ur wondering, like, "is there some secret beyond this," some mystique... the answer is no

if u can score 100/100 on that framework u have as good a shot as anyone

and with LLMs theres no reason why u cant get damn close.

bon courage 😎
